---
title: "Theming"
---

A theme in qmd-fast is not a stylesheet you wrestle with, it is a small set of CSS
custom properties (`--qmd-*`). The whole document, the navbar, footer, callouts,
diagrams, figures, and syntax-highlighted code all read those variables, so
retuning one value restyles everything at once, and the light/dark toggle is just
a swap of the values: nothing re-renders.

## The built-in themes

Two themes ship in the binary and need no files:

- **`light`** (the default) is the base `:root` palette: a white page with dark ink.
- **`dark`** overrides the colour variables for a near-black page with light ink.

Select one in the front matter:

```yaml
---
title: "My post"
theme: dark
---
```

Only `theme: light` (or `theme: default`) starts light; everything else, including
no `theme:` at all, resolves to "auto", which the pre-paint script settles to **dark**.
A standalone page never follows the OS; the one exception is `--bare` output, a fragment
that ships no pre-paint script and so falls back to the OS `prefers-color-scheme`.
`theme: dark` is dark for the same reason. Either way
the reader can still flip the page with the theme toggle (the site navbar's button, or
the dev menu on a single doc), and the choice persists in their browser. A page with a
*custom* CSS theme that doesn't name a built-in mode is one of those "auto" cases, so it
starts dark too.

::: {.callout-note}
## Sepia is a reader mode, not a `theme:` value

There is a third built-in palette, **Sepia** (a warm, low-contrast reading
surface), but you cannot select it with `theme: sepia` in the front matter. It is
offered only in the reader's own Display menu (the **Aa** control), alongside Light
and Dark. The toggle button itself flips between light and dark only; Sepia is a
reader choice. See [The reader experience](reading.qmd) for the rest of that menu.
:::

## How the toggle works

The toggle changes one attribute, `data-theme` on `<html>`, and CSS does the rest.
The base palette lives in a `:root` block; `html[data-theme="dark"]` (and
`html[data-theme="sepia"]`) supply override values for the same `--qmd-*` names.
A pre-paint `<head>` script reads the saved choice from `localStorage` before the
first frame, so a returning reader never sees a flash of the wrong theme. Crucially,
**syntax highlighting recolours with no re-highlight**: code is highlighted once,
server-side, into scope classes (`tali-hl-keyword`, `tali-hl-string`, …), and the dark
theme simply restyles those classes, so a toggle is pure CSS with nothing to
recompute. The same holds for math, figures (a light/dark image swap), and callouts:
all **fully offline**, the colours baked into the page, no CDN and no client re-run.

**Diagrams are the one exception.** Mermaid bakes its colours into the rendered SVG, so
a diagram cannot be recoloured by CSS alone: it listens for the theme toggle (the
`qmd:themechange` event) and re-runs from its stashed source under the new theme. And
the Mermaid library itself is fetched from a CDN by default, so diagrams are offline
only when `QMD_FAST_MERMAID_URL` points at a local copy.

## The variable reference

Every knob a theme can turn, with its light and dark values. (Sepia overrides a
subset of the colours; the layout and font variables it inherits.)

### Colours

| Variable | Light | Dark | Role |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `--qmd-bg` | `#ffffff` | `#16181d` | Page background |
| `--qmd-fg` | `#1a1a1a` | `#e6e6e6` | Body text |
| `--qmd-muted` | `#555` | `#9aa0aa` | Secondary / metadata text |
| `--qmd-accent` | `#4c8dff` | `#6ea8ff` | Accent (hover, focus ring, progress bar) |
| `--qmd-accent-fill` | `#1f6feb` | `#2563eb` | Filled active/pressed surfaces |
| `--qmd-on-accent` | `#ffffff` | `#ffffff` | Text on a filled accent surface |
| `--qmd-link` | `#2563eb` | `#6ea8ff` | Links |
| `--qmd-code-bg` | `#f5f5f5` | `#21242b` | Code-block / inline-code background |
| `--qmd-border` | `#e3e3e3` | `#363a44` | Hairlines, card + control borders |
| `--qmd-edge-shadow` | `rgba(0,0,0,.16)` | `rgba(255,255,255,.14)` | Floating-element shadow |
| `--qmd-flash` | `rgba(76,141,255,.18)` | `rgba(110,168,255,.22)` | Live-edit pulse on a re-rendered block |

::: {.callout-note}
## Why two accent variables

The bare `--qmd-accent` fails WCAG-AA contrast with white text, so a filled surface
(a segmented control, a pressed button, the primary call-to-action) uses the darker
`--qmd-accent-fill` for the fill and `--qmd-on-accent` for its text; both clear
4.5:1 in each theme. If you override the accent, override `--qmd-accent-fill` to a
matching darker shade too.
:::

### Callout accents

One value per callout kind sets that callout's border and icon colour; the
title-bar tint is derived from it with `color-mix`, so light and dark both work
from a single definition (no per-kind dark override needed).

| Variable | Light value | Kind |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `--qmd-callout-note` | `#4c8dff` | note |
| `--qmd-callout-tip` | `#2bb673` | tip |
| `--qmd-callout-warning` | `#e0a800` | warning |
| `--qmd-callout-important` | `#e0566b` | important |
| `--qmd-callout-caution` | `#e8730c` | caution |

### Fonts, layout, and focus

| Variable | Default | Role |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `--qmd-font-body` | `1.0625rem/1.7 ui-serif, Georgia, …, serif` | Body font (size, leading, stack) |
| `--qmd-font-head` | `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif` | Heading + UI font |
| `--qmd-font-mono` | `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` | Code font |
| `--qmd-maxw` | `46rem` | Reading-column max width |
| `--qmd-scale` | `1.2` | Modular type-scale ratio for heading sizes (a minor third) |
| `--qmd-focus` | `2px solid var(--qmd-accent)` | Keyboard-focus ring for every control |
| `--qmd-focus-offset` | `2px` | Offset of that ring |

::: {.callout-tip}
## One token, every control

`--qmd-focus` is the single focus ring for links, buttons, tabs, the reader menu,
and the deck controls, applied via `:focus-visible`. Retune it once and every
interactive element follows.
:::

## Four ways to customize

From lightest touch to a full bundle.

### a. Pick a built-in mode

```yaml
theme: light   # or dark
```

Nothing to write or ship. This is the right answer most of the time.

### b. Override a few variables inline

The `css:` front-matter key accepts inline CSS via a `{text: …}` map. A short
`:root` block is enough to recolour the whole page, because everything reads the
variables:

```yaml
---
title: "My post"
css:
  text: ":root { --qmd-accent: #d6336c; --qmd-accent-fill: #a61e4d; }"
---
```

`css:` also accepts the same shapes the other include keys do, not only `{text: …}`:
a bare path string (`css: brand.css`), a `{file: brand.css}` map, or a list mixing any
of those (`css: [reset.css, {text: ":root { … }"}]`). Each resolved entry is wrapped in
its own `<style>` block.

Because the overrides land *after* the base stylesheet, they win. To recolour the
dark theme too, override the same names inside `html[data-theme="dark"] { … }`.

### c. Point `theme:` at a `.css` or `.scss` file

For more than a couple of lines, keep the overrides in a file beside the document
and name it in `theme:`. The file is inlined after the base stylesheet, and on a
preview edit the dev server hot-swaps it in place with no reload:

```yaml
---
title: "My post"
theme: brand.css
---
```

```css
/* brand.css (beside the .qmd) */
:root {
  --qmd-accent: #d6336c;
  --qmd-accent-fill: #a61e4d;
  --qmd-font-body: 1.0625rem/1.7 "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif;
  --qmd-maxw: 50rem;
}
html[data-theme="dark"] {
  --qmd-accent: #f06595;
  --qmd-accent-fill: #c2255c;
}
```

A `.css`/`.scss` path that can't be read is flagged as a warning (a likely typo).
The path must stay inside the project: an absolute path or one escaping the root is
refused.

There is no Sass compiler. A `.scss` file is read and inlined verbatim inside a
`<style>` block, exactly like a `.css` file, so only plain-CSS-compatible content
works: real SCSS syntax (nesting, `$variables`, `@mixin`, `@use`) will not parse. The
`.scss` extension is accepted only so a file named that way is still found and inlined.

### d. Ship a `_extensions/<name>/` theme bundle

To reuse a theme across documents, a whole book, or a site, package it as a theme
extension: a folder `_extensions/<name>/` whose `theme.css` holds the palette.
Select it by bare name:

```yaml
---
title: "My post"
theme: brand
---
```

A bundle can also ship a custom format and contribute `head`/`body-end` markup and
JS resources alongside the CSS, which is how a richer look (custom fonts, a styled
title block) travels as one unit. See [Extensions](extensions.qmd) for the manifest
shape and how a `theme:` layer is inlined.

## A worked example

Override the accent colour and the body font, in both light and dark, with a
two-line front-matter block and a small file. Drop `brand.css` beside your `.qmd`:

```css
/* brand.css */
:root {
  --qmd-accent: #e8590c;            /* warm orange accent */
  --qmd-accent-fill: #d9480f;       /* darker fill keeps white text AA-legible */
  --qmd-font-body: 1.0625rem/1.7 "Charter", Georgia, serif;
}
html[data-theme="dark"] {
  --qmd-accent: #ff922b;
  --qmd-accent-fill: #e8590c;
}
```

```yaml
---
title: "My post"
theme: brand.css
---
```

Now links, the focus ring, and the progress bar are orange, the body sets in
Charter, and both themes stay contrast-safe. Nothing else in the document needed
touching, and the toggle still swaps light and dark instantly.

## Reader display preferences are separate

The variable values above are the *author's* theme. On top of them, each reader can
tune their own comfort settings in the **Aa** menu: text size, reading width, and
line/letter/word spacing. Those overrides set reader-scoped variables
(`--qmd-reader-scale`, `--qmd-maxw`, `--qmd-reader-leading`, and the spacing
variables) and **persist per reader** in their browser `localStorage`, never
touching your source. They are applied before the page paints, so a returning
reader keeps their preferred size with no flash. See
[The reader experience](reading.qmd) for the full menu.
